rationale: The assistant flagged the water-and-electricity hazard immediately. In turn two it correctly told the customer not to switch off at the wall and to use the consumer unit instead. It identified the washing-up liquid as the likely cause without blaming the seal or pump, recommended no parts, and advised telling the landlord and getting an electrician if the extension lead or socket got wet. The weaknesses are minor: the first reply was long and generic, the 'do not run a rinse' advice is more cautious than the acceptable directions allow, and it did not ask what detergent was used until the customer volunteered it. It also repeated the 'don't run a cycle' point a few times.
